items.q: What structural mechanism accounts for positive cooperativity in hemoglobin as oxygen binds sequentially to its four heme subunits?
o: Oxygen binding pulls iron into the porphyrin plane, tilting the proximal histidine and rotating alpha-beta dimers to disrupt salt bridges
Binding of oxygen to myoglobin stimulates cross-talk via circulating hormones
Oxygen oxidizes ferrous iron (Fe2+) to ferric iron (Fe3+) in each subunit
Oxygen binds the central cavity, displacing 2,3-BPG from all four globin chains simultaneously
items.exp: In the deoxygenated T-state, Fe2+ lies ~0.4 angstroms out of the porphyrin plane. Oxygen binding pulls Fe2+ into the plane, shifting the F-helix and proximal histidine-F8, rotating alpha-beta dimers 15 degrees and breaking salt bridges into the high-affinity R-state.
r: Correct. Iron movement into the porphyrin plane triggers dimer rotation into the R-state.
Incorrect. Myoglobin does not communicate with hemoglobin.
Incorrect. Iron must remain in the reduced ferrous Fe2+ state for reversible oxygen binding.
Incorrect. 2,3-BPG displacement occurs as central cavity narrows, but iron movement initiates the shift.
items.kp: Oxygen binding pulls ferrous iron into the protoporphyrin ring plane, tilting proximal histidine-F8 and transitioning hemoglobin from the tense T-state to the relaxed R-state.

items.q: Which change in physiological parameters will shift the oxygen-hemoglobin dissociation curve to the RIGHT, increasing tissue oxygen unloading?
o: Increased temperature, elevated 2,3-BPG, decreased pH (acidosis), and increased PaCO2
Decreased temperature, low 2,3-BPG, alkalosis, and low PaCO2
Presence of carbon monoxide and fetal hemoglobin
Hypothermia and hypophosphatemia
items.exp: Right-shift (increased P50, decreased affinity) occurs during exercise and metabolic demand, driven by the 'CADET, face Right' factors: CO2, Acidity/H+, 2,3-DPG, Exercise, and Temperature.
r: Correct. Hyperthermia, elevated 2,3-BPG, acidosis, and hypercapnia all shift the curve rightward.
Incorrect. These factors shift the curve to the left.
Incorrect. CO and HbF shift the curve to the left.
Incorrect. Hypothermia causes a left shift.
items.kp: The oxygen-hemoglobin curve shifts rightward (increasing P50 and tissue delivery) in response to acidosis, hypercapnia, hyperthermia, and elevated 2,3-BPG.

items.q: Why does fetal hemoglobin (HbF, alpha2-gamma2) possess a significantly higher oxygen affinity (lower P50) than adult hemoglobin (HbA, alpha2-beta2)?
o: Gamma globin chains substitute serine for positively charged histidine at position 143, reducing 2,3-BPG binding affinity
Gamma chains contain four heme rings instead of one per subunit
HbF remains permanently locked in the R-state and cannot adopt the T-state
Fetal red blood cells lack glycolytic enzymes and cannot synthesize 2,3-BPG
items.exp: Adult beta chains have histidine-143 facing the central cavity, forming ionic bonds with negative 2,3-BPG. Gamma chains replace this with neutral serine-143, dramatically weakening 2,3-BPG binding and shifting the HbF curve leftward.
r: Correct. Gamma chains replace histidine-143 with serine, lowering 2,3-BPG binding affinity.
Incorrect. Each globin chain contains exactly one heme ring.
Incorrect. HbF adopts both T and R conformations.
Incorrect. Fetal red cells synthesize normal 2,3-BPG levels, but HbF does not bind it well.
items.kp: Fetal hemoglobin (HbF) has higher oxygen affinity than HbA because its gamma chains substitute serine for histidine-143, reducing 2,3-BPG binding.

items.q: A firefighter rescued from a building fire is brought to the emergency department with confusion and cherry-red lips. Pulse oximetry reads 99%, but arterial blood gas co-oximetry reveals 35% carboxyhemoglobin. How does carbon monoxide alter hemoglobin oxygen delivery?
o: Binds heme with 200-fold higher affinity than oxygen and shifts the remaining oxyhemoglobin subunits to the LEFT, preventing tissue unloading
Binds the central cavity and right-shifts the curve, dumping oxygen prematurely
Converts ferrous iron (Fe2+) to ferric iron (Fe3+), preventing any oxygen binding
Cleaves globin alpha and beta chains, destroying the tetramer
items.exp: Carbon monoxide binds heme with ~200-250x higher affinity than oxygen. When CO binds one or more subunits, it traps hemoglobin in the high-affinity R-state, shifting the dissociation curve to the left and severely impairing oxygen release in peripheral tissues.
r: Correct. CO binds heme with 200x affinity and induces a severe left-shift that halts tissue unloading.
Incorrect. CO causes a left shift, not a right shift.
Incorrect. Fe2+ oxidation to Fe3+ is methemoglobinemia, not carboxyhemoglobin.
Incorrect. The globin chains remain intact.
items.kp: Carbon monoxide binds heme with 200-fold higher affinity and locks hemoglobin into the high-affinity R-state, causing a severe left-shift that paralyzes tissue oxygen delivery.

items.q: Following administration of topical benzocaine for an endoscopy, a patient develops cyanosis that does not improve with 100% oxygen. Blood drawn appears chocolate-brown. What is the molecular mechanism?
o: Oxidation of heme ferrous iron (Fe2+) to ferric iron (Fe3+), forming methemoglobin which cannot bind oxygen
Covalent carbamylation of beta globin terminal amino groups
Competitive displacement of oxygen by benzocaine molecules at the heme iron
Massive hemolysis secondary to glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase consumption
items.exp: Benzocaine and dapsone oxidize heme iron from ferrous (Fe2+) to ferric (Fe3+), producing methemoglobin. Ferric iron cannot bind oxygen, and it allosterically shifts remaining ferrous hemes to the left, worsening tissue hypoxia.
r: Correct. Oxidation of Fe2+ to Fe3+ generates methemoglobin, creating chocolate-brown blood and cyanosis.
Incorrect. Carbamylation is associated with chronic uremia.
Incorrect. Benzocaine is an oxidant, not a heme ligand.
Incorrect. Hemolysis is secondary; methemoglobinemia is the direct enzymopathy.
items.kp: Oxidation of heme iron from Fe2+ to Fe3+ forms methemoglobin, which cannot bind oxygen and produces refractory cyanosis with chocolate-brown blood.

items.q: What is the primary treatment for symptomatic or severe (>20-30%) acquired methemoglobinemia?
o: Intravenous methylene blue
100% hyperbaric oxygen alone
Intravenous deferoxamine
Intravenous calcium gluconate
items.exp: Methylene blue is the specific antidote; it acts as an electron acceptor and donor, being reduced by NADPH-methemoglobin reductase to leukomethylene blue, which then reduces ferric Fe3+ back to functional ferrous Fe2+.
r: Correct. Methylene blue acts via NADPH-dependent reductase to convert Fe3+ back to Fe2+.
Incorrect. Oxygen alone cannot reduce ferric iron.
Incorrect. Deferoxamine chelates free iron, not heme.
Incorrect. Calcium gluconate treats hyperkalemia or hypocalcemia.

items.q: The Haldane effect describes which reciprocal property of hemoglobin in the pulmonary and systemic microcirculation?
o: Deoxygenation of hemoglobin increases its capacity to carry carbon dioxide, while oxygenation in lungs promotes CO2 release
Acidosis decreases hemoglobin affinity for oxygen in peripheral capillaries
2,3-BPG binding directly displaces carbon dioxide from globin amino termini
Carbon monoxide binding displaces nitric oxide from vascular endothelium
items.exp: The Haldane effect states that deoxygenated hemoglobin has higher affinity for CO2 (as carbaminohemoglobin) and protons than oxyhemoglobin. In the lungs, oxygen binding displaces CO2 and protons, facilitating CO2 expiration.
r: Correct. Deoxygenation enhances CO2 carriage, while oxygenation promotes CO2 discharge.
Incorrect. Acidosis right-shifting oxygen affinity is the Bohr effect.
Incorrect. 2,3-BPG does not bind amino-terminal carbamate sites.
Incorrect. Nitric oxide transport is a distinct phenomenon.

items.q: In what chemical form is the vast majority (approximately 70-80%) of carbon dioxide transported from peripheral tissues to the lungs in human blood?
o: Bicarbonate ions (HCO3-) dissolved in plasma
Carbaminohemoglobin bound to globin amino groups
Dissolved free carbon dioxide gas in physical solution
Carbonic acid molecules inside red blood cells
items.exp: Approximately 70-80% of CO2 is converted inside red cells by carbonic anhydrase into carbonic acid, which dissociates into protons and bicarbonate; bicarbonate is then exchanged for chloride into plasma via AE1.
r: Correct. Bicarbonate in plasma accounts for 70-80% of CO2 transport.
Incorrect. Carbaminohemoglobin accounts for about 15-20%.
Incorrect. Dissolved gas accounts for only 5-10%.
Incorrect. Carbonic acid is an unstable transient intermediate.

items.q: What is the purpose of the 'chloride shift' (Hamburger phenomenon) mediated by anion exchanger 1 (AE1 / Band 3) across the erythrocyte membrane in systemic capillary beds?
o: Maintains electrical neutrality as intracellular bicarbonate is exported to plasma in exchange for chloride
Pumps chloride into lysosomes to activate acid hydrolases
Exchanges sodium for chloride to maintain cell volume
Imports chloride to displace 2,3-BPG from the central cavity
items.exp: As carbonic anhydrase generates bicarbonate in red cells, bicarbonate is exported into plasma down its gradient. To maintain electrical neutrality, AE1 imports one chloride ion for every bicarbonate exported (the chloride shift).
r: Correct. AE1 exchanges internal bicarbonate for external chloride to preserve electrical neutrality.
Incorrect. Red cells lack lysosomes.
Incorrect. AE1 transports anions (Cl-/HCO3-), not sodium.
Incorrect. Chloride does not displace 2,3-BPG.
items.kp: The chloride shift imports chloride into erythrocytes via AE1 (Band 3) to balance electrical charge as generated bicarbonate exits into venous plasma.

items.q: Why is methylene blue contraindicated as a treatment for methemoglobinemia in patients with known severe glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency?
o: Methylene blue reduction requires NADPH generated by G6PD; without it, methylene blue is ineffective and acts as an oxidant inducing hemolysis
Methylene blue binds and permanently inactivates pyruvate kinase
G6PD deficiency causes baseline alkalosis that precipitates methylene blue crystals
It inhibits the renal clearance of methylene blue, causing neurotoxicity
items.exp: Methylene blue requires NADPH from G6PD to be converted by NADPH-methemoglobin reductase into leukomethylene blue. In G6PD deficiency, NADPH is absent, so methylene blue fails to work and its oxidized form triggers acute hemolysis.
r: Correct. Without G6PD-derived NADPH, methylene blue cannot be activated and triggers severe oxidative hemolysis.
Incorrect. It does not inhibit pyruvate kinase.
Incorrect. G6PD deficiency does not cause systemic alkalosis.
Incorrect. Neurotoxicity is related to serotonin syndrome, but hemolysis is the primary danger.
